target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial air transport under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports six fatal hull-loss accidents involving Western-built jets in 2013. The annual accident annex maps the relevant fatal jet set to SCAT CRJ, National Airlines B747, Asiana B777, UPS A300, Tatarstan B737 and LAM EMB-190. Of these six, National, Asiana and Tatarstan are Boeing aircraft; SCAT, UPS and LAM are non-Boeing.

evidence.source_title: 2013 Statistical Summary of Commercial Jet Airplane Accidents
evidence.scope: worldwide commercial jet fleet under documented Boeing rules
evidence.observation: Boeing's 2013 table independently records National Air Cargo Group 747-400 as a fatal scheduled-cargo accident and provides the worldwide commercial-jet reconciliation surface; the IATA annual census supplies the independent complete fatal-jet mapping used for the six-control audit.

completeness_assessment.reason: The IATA annual global commercial-aviation census identifies six fatal Western-built jet accidents and maps all six manufacturers. Exactly three are Boeing: National 747, Asiana 777 and Tatarstan 737. Each Boeing candidate has competent accident-investigation evidence and independent annual reconciliation, with no unresolved hostile-action, missing-aircraft or external-fatality target boundary affecting 2013 membership.
